title: Chess
how_to_play: A unified platform for 155 chess variants spanning classic FIDE rules, asymmetric battles, hidden information, expanded boards, alternative win conditions, regional forms, and topology variants. Every variant shares the chess lineage but modifies setup, pieces, board, or victory condition.

variants.title: Alice Chess
variants.board: Two 8×8 boards (Board A and Board B)
variants.special: After every move, the moving piece transfers to the corresponding square on the other board. A move is only legal if the transfer square is vacant. Invented V. R. Parton, 1953.

variants.title: Standard Grasshopper Chess
variants.special: Each queen is replaced by a Grasshopper — a piece that must hop over a hurdle to move.

variants.title: Gygax Chess
variants.special: Three stacked 12×8 boards. 42 pieces per side across 15 piece types. Air, Land, and Subterranean realms. Gary Gygax, Dragon Magazine No. 100, 1985.

variants.title: Standard Nightrider Chess
variants.special: Knights are replaced by Nightriders — riders that chain knight-leaps in a single direction.

variants.title: Standard Chess
variants.special: Standard FIDE rules

variants.title: Standard Wildebeest Chess
variants.special: An 11×10 board. Camels replace bishops; Wildebeests (Knight+Camel compound) flank the queen.

variants.title: Absorption Chess
variants.special: Capturing piece permanently gains the victim's movement abilities. Absorptions stack.

variants.title: Almost Chess
variants.special: White's Queen is replaced by a Chancellor (Rook + Knight compound).

variants.title: Amazon Chess
variants.special: Queens replaced by Amazons (Queen + Knight). The most powerful piece possible.

variants.title: Andernach Chess
variants.special: Capturing piece changes colour (becomes opponent's). Kings exempt.

variants.title: Anti-King Chess II
variants.win: Checkmate the opponent's King or Anti-King
variants.special: Each player adds an Anti-King — a royal piece in check whenever it is NOT attacked by enemy pieces. Win by checkmating either the King or the Anti-King. Anti-Kings cannot capture enemy pieces.

variants.title: Antichess
variants.win: Lose all pieces or get stalemated
variants.special: Captures are mandatory. First to lose all pieces wins.

variants.title: Archchess
variants.special: 10×10 chess variant by Dr. Francesco Piacenza (Turin, 1683). Adds two new pieces per side: the Centurion (Dabbaba + Alfil + Knight compound; can jump) and the Decurion (one square diagonally). Pawns always promote to Queen. Unusual flexible castling rules including a King’s Leap option.

variants.title: ASEAN Chess
variants.special: Standardized Southeast Asian chess for regional competition. Makruk-family rules: Bishop moves 1 step diagonally, Pawns start on rank 2, promote on rank 6 to Ferz. Streamlined counting draw rules. Codified by ASEAN Chess Federation.

variants.title: Atomic Chess
variants.special: Captures cause explosions destroying all pieces on adjacent squares.

variants.title: Avalanche Chess
variants.special: Each turn has two parts: first make a legal chess move, then push one of the opponent's pawns one square forward. The push is obligatory. If pushing a pawn leaves your King in check, you lose immediately.

variants.title: Balbo's Chess
variants.board: Diamond-shaped, 70 squares (ranks 3-5-7-9-11-11-9-7-5-3, centred on file f)
variants.special: Chess on an unusual diamond-shaped board invented by M.G. Balbo (1974). Ten ranks of widths 3-5-7-9-11-11-9-7-5-3, all centred on file f, giving 70 squares across files a-k. Promotion rules are location-dependent: corner promotion squares allow minor pieces only. Pritchard warns that both sides have a third-move mate available from the starting position.

variants.title: Benedict Chess
variants.special: No captures. Attacked enemies convert to your colour instead.

variants.title: Berolina Chess
variants.special: Pawns move diagonally forward and capture straight forward — the inverse of normal.

variants.title: Berserk Chess
variants.special: Delivering check grants one bonus move with a different piece.

variants.title: Bird's Chess
variants.special: 1874 variant on a 10×8 board. Adds Guard (Rook+Knight) and Equerry (Bishop+Knight). A predecessor to Capablanca’s Chess. Castling: King moves three squares, Rook jumps over to the adjacent square.

variants.title: Blind Chess (Banqi)
variants.win: Capture all opponent's face-up pieces (opponent with no legal moves loses)
variants.special: Chinese hidden-piece game (Banqi, 暗棋) played on a 4×8 board (half a Xiangqi board). All 32 pieces placed face-down randomly. Each turn: flip a piece, move a piece, or capture. Piece ranks are unknown until revealed. Capture hierarchy: General defeats all except Soldier; Soldier defeats General. Cannon captures by jumping over exactly one screen (Taiwanese rules).

variants.title: Breakthrough
variants.special: Pawns only — first to reach the far side wins. No captures backward.

variants.title: Brusky's Hexagonal Chess
variants.special: Horizontal 84-hex board. 10 pawns per side. Unmoved pawns may also capture straight forward. Blockage rule applies. Invented Yakov Brusky.

variants.title: Byzantine Chess
variants.win: Checkmate, stalemate the opponent, or bare the opponent's King
variants.special: Played on a circular board of 4 concentric rings and 16 files (64 squares). Uses Shatranj piece movements: Bishops leap two diagonal squares, Queens move one diagonal square. Stalemate is a win. Baring the opponent's King wins unless the opponent can bare back immediately.

variants.title: Capablanca Chess
variants.special: Two extra pieces: Archbishop (B+N) and Chancellor (R+N). Wider board.

variants.title: Carrera's Chess
variants.special: 1617 historical variant on a 10×8 board. Adds Champion (Rook+Knight) and Centaur (Bishop+Knight). No castling, no en passant. A pawn double move is forbidden if it would both block a check and pass through an enemy pawn’s capture square.

variants.title: Centennial Chess
variants.special: 10×10 chess variant with four new pieces: the Steward (quadra-pawn, moves as pawn in all 4 directions), the Camel (2+1 oblique leap, colorbound), the Murray Lion (leaps to 2nd square orthogonally/diagonally or captures as King), and the Rotating Spearman (slides forward/backward and rotates between 3 orientations). Two moves per turn until first capture. En passant disabled. Created by John William Brown, 1999. Entry in the 1999 Large Variant Contest.

variants.title: Chak
variants.special: Mesoamerican-themed chess on a 9×9 board. Win by mating the Ajaw or landing your promoted Ajaw on the opponent's temple square. Pieces promote when crossing the river. Designed by Corey Clark, 2020.

variants.title: Chancellor Chess
variants.special: 9×9 chess variant published by Ben Foster (1889). Adds one Chancellor (Rook+Knight compound) per side, placed to the right of the King. Black squares are in the corners. Castling: King moves 2 squares, Rook moves 3. Pawns may promote to Chancellor.

variants.title: Chaturanga
variants.special: Ancient Indian ancestor of all chess variants, c. 600 CE. Weak counsellor and leaping elephant.

variants.title: Checkless Chess
variants.special: Cannot give check unless it is checkmate. King becomes aggressive.

variants.title: Chennis
variants.special: Tennis-themed chess on a 7×7 board. Win by advancing a Pawn to the opponent's back rank. A net across rank 4 prevents most pieces from crossing. Knights may jump the net freely. Designed by Corey Clark.

variants.title: Chigorin
variants.special: White's Bishops replaced by Knights. Four Knights vs standard army.

variants.title: Circular Chess
variants.special: Played on a circular board of 64 squares arranged in 4 concentric rings of 16 files. No castling, no en passant. Pawns promote after travelling 6 squares. Null moves (moving a piece all the way around a ring back to its start) are illegal.

variants.title: Citadel Chess
variants.win: Checkmate or stalemate; reaching the opponent's citadel is a draw
variants.special: Historical Shatranj variant (Shatranj al-Husun, 'Chess of the Fortresses'). 10×10 board plus four corner citadel squares. A King entering the opponent's citadel and surviving one move achieves a draw. Stalemate is a win. War Machines move as Bishops. No bare King rule.

variants.title: Codrus
variants.special: No check exists. You win by getting your own King captured.

variants.title: Congo
variants.special: 7×7 chess variant by Demian Freeling (1982, age 7). Six unique piece types: Lion (King, confined to castle), Zebra (Knight), Giraffe (2-step jump + king move), Elephant (1–2 step ortho leaper), Crocodile (king move + rook toward/in river), Monkey (capturing draughts-leaper). River rank in the centre. Drowning rule: non-Crocodile pieces left in the river for a full turn are removed. No check or checkmate — capture the Lion to win.

variants.title: Courier Chess
variants.special: Medieval German variant from 1202. Courier (modern bishop), Mann, Schleich (orthogonal-only), and Alfil on a 12-wide board.

variants.title: Crazy 38's
variants.win: Checkmate the opponent's King OR move your King to the opponent's Home Square
variants.special: 38-square chess variant by Ben Good, entered in the 1998 38 Squares Contest. Uses Shogi-style drops. Unique piece set: King, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Silver General, Gold General, and 4 Pawns per side — with movements distinct from standard Shogi. The board has a built-in loop connection that Rooks can exploit. Pawns promote to Queen only on the opponent's Home Square; captured Queens revert to Pawns before being dropped. Dual win condition: checkmate OR King reaches opponent's Home Square.

variants.title: Crazyhouse
variants.special: Captured pieces switch sides and can be dropped back onto the board.

variants.title: Cylinder Chess
variants.special: Files wrap — the a-file connects to the h-file. Pieces slide around the cylinder.

variants.title: Cylindrical Chess
variants.special: The board is treated as a cylinder: file a connects directly to file h. Pieces can move and attack across the edge. Bishops and queens are significantly stronger than in standard chess.

variants.title: Dark Chess
variants.special: Total fog — only see squares occupied by your own pieces.

variants.title: De Vasa's Hexagonal Chess
variants.special: Horizontally-oriented rhombus board of 81 hexes. Pawns start on rank 3. Castling permitted. Invented Helge E. de Vasa.

variants.title: Delirious Bughouse
variants.win: Capture an opposing King (team loses if either ally's King is captured)
variants.special: Bughouse variant by Alberto Monteiro (c.1984) combining relay capture, dice, and a worst-move mechanic. Two boards, 4 players, 2 allied teams. Key Bughouse modifications: Pawns drop only on ranks 2–6 (not rank 7); promoted Pawns when captured stay promoted (the promoting player recovers the original Pawn, permanently increasing piece count). Add-on layers: Dice Chess (die each turn — 1=Pawn, 2=Knight, 3=Bishop, 4=Rook, 5=Queen, 6=any); Worst Move (second die determines whether the player or opponent chooses the move); fairy pieces (Camel, Giraffe, Zebra, Cylindrical pieces, Pyramid, Atomic Bomb). Final full form adds Structures, Events, and Magic Items.

variants.title: Diana Chess
variants.special: 6×6 board. No queens or knights — bishops and rooks only.

variants.title: Dice Chess
variants.special: Die roll constrains which piece type must move.

variants.title: Displacement Chess
variants.special: Pieces can swap positions with adjacent friendly pieces as an alternative move.

variants.title: Djambi
variants.win: Be the last player with a Chief remaining
variants.special: 4-player political strategy on a 9×9 grid. Killed pieces remain as impassable corpses; the center Maze grants extra turns and immunities.

variants.title: Dragon Chess
variants.special: Created by Grandmaster Miguel Illescas. Standard chess with two Dragons (Bishop+Knight = Archbishop) held in reserve; at any point instead of a move, gate one onto any empty square on your own first rank.

variants.title: Duck Chess
variants.special: After each move, place the duck (blocker) on any empty square.

variants.title: Einstein Chess
variants.special: Non-capturing moves demote pieces; captures promote them (Q→R→B→N→P / P→N→B→R→Q).

variants.title: Empire Chess
variants.special: Asymmetric: FIDE Kingdom vs. Empire dynasty. Empire pieces move like Queens but capture in limited piece-specific ways. Faceoff rule: open-file confrontation between royal pieces loses for the creator. Designed by Couch Tomato, 2020.

variants.title: Endgame Chess
variants.special: Only Kings and pawns. Pure endgame technique from move one.

variants.title: Extinction Chess
variants.win: Capture all of one piece type
variants.special: Lose all your knights, bishops, rooks, or pawns — you lose the game.

variants.title: Fanorona Chess
variants.special: Chess variant on the double Alquerque board used in Fanorona (the traditional Malagasy game of Madagascar). Captures are by approach and withdrawal, not replacement: moving toward an enemy piece captures it; moving away from an enemy piece also captures it. If a capture is available, it must be made. Stalemate is a loss. No castling; no en passant; Pawn promotes only to previously captured pieces. Created by Peter Aronson, 2004.

variants.title: Fischer Random (Chess960)
variants.special: Back rank pieces randomised (960 positions). Castling rules adapted.

variants.title: Five-Check
variants.special: Extended Three-Check — five checks wins instead of three.

variants.title: Flip Chess
variants.special: Chess variant on a 38-square board with an unusual shape. 'Bare king loses' — a player whose King is the only piece remaining loses immediately, regardless of whether they are in check. No initial double Pawn moves. Companion to Crazy 38's (both are 38-square chess variants by John William Brown). Acclaimed 38-square variant; Java applet implementation by Ed Friedlander on chessvariants.com. Created 1999.

variants.title: Fog of War Chess
variants.special: You only see squares your pieces can move to. No check warnings.

variants.title: Four-Handed Chess (Chaturaji)
variants.win: Accumulate the most points from captures; 54 points for capturing all three enemy Kings
variants.special: Ancient Indian 4-player dice chess (c. 1030 CE). No checkmate — Kings are captured for points. Dice determine which piece type moves.

variants.title: Giveaway
variants.special: Forced captures. King is not royal. Stalemate is a loss.

variants.title: Glinski's Hexagonal Chess
variants.special: Chess on a 91-cell hexagonal board. Pieces slide along hex edges and vertices. Three bishops per side (one per cell colour).

variants.title: Grand Chess
variants.special: Marshal and Cardinal on a 10×10 board, pawns start on rank 3.

variants.title: Grande Acedrex
variants.win: Checkmate, bare the King, or stalemate
variants.special: Large medieval Spanish chess variant from the Libro de los Juegos (Alfonso X, c. 1283). 12×12 board with six unique piece types: Griffion, Unicorn, Lion, Giraffe, Crocodile, and Rook. Pawns start on rank 4; ranks 2–3 are empty. Unique promotion rule: pawn promotes to the piece type that started on that file.

variants.title: Grid Chess
variants.special: Moves must cross at least one 2×2 grid line.

variants.title: Gustav III's Chess
variants.special: Swedish historical chess variant also known as Shakspel. Standard 8×8 chess with four extra squares added at the corners, each occupied by an Amazon (a piece combining Queen and Knight moves). Each side has 2 Amazons in addition to the standard FIDE army. Created by Gustav Johan Billberg, 1839. Jocly implementation available on chessvariants.com.

variants.title: Half Chess
variants.special: 4-rank board, armies start adjacent. Immediate contact.

variants.title: Hexapawn
variants.win: Advance a Pawn to the last rank, OR leave opponent with no legal moves
variants.special: 3×3 pawn-only game invented by Martin Gardner (Scientific American, March 1962) as a teaching tool for minimax strategy and machine learning. Six pawns total (3 per side). Solved game: Black wins with perfect play. No double-step; reaching the far rank wins immediately.

variants.title: Hole Chess
variants.win: Capture or checkmate the opponent's King
variants.special: 44-square chess variant on a custom board with two permanent holes — squares pieces cannot occupy, but through which pieces can be 'sucked.' The Queen, Rook, and PS-Bishop (Dragon Horse) each have a Two-Action Rule: they may move normally AND pull an enemy piece in their line of fire into a hole on the same turn. Named for the 44-square contest. Gary K. Gifford, 2003.

variants.title: Hoppel-Poppel
variants.special: Knights capture like bishops (sliding diagonal); bishops capture like knights (L-jump).

variants.title: Horde Chess
variants.win: White checkmates or Black destroys horde
variants.special: White has a full army. Black has 36 pawns. Asymmetric survival.

variants.title: Hostage Chess
variants.special: Shogi-inspired drop variant using a single standard set. Captured pieces become "hostages"; you can rescue yours by releasing one of theirs. Promoted pawns are replaced by prison pieces. Named chess variant of the decade by David Pritchard (Variant Chess, Summer 1999).

variants.title: Immunization Chess
variants.special: When a capture occurs, adjacent enemy pieces become immune to capture for 2 turns.

variants.title: Janus Chess
variants.special: Played on a 10×8 board. Each player adds two Januses (Archbishop: Bishop + Knight combined) between the Rooks and Knights. Castling sends the King to the b-file (3 squares) or i-file (4 squares).

variants.title: Khan's Chess
variants.special: Asymmetric: White plays FIDE chess, Gold commands the Mongol Horde — all Horde pieces except Khan and Kheshig are divergent (move ≠ capture). Stalemate is a loss. Campmate wins (King to opponent's back rank).

variants.title: King of the Hill
variants.win: Checkmate or king reaches centre 4 squares
variants.special: Moving your king to d4/d5/e4/e5 is an instant win.

variants.title: Klein Bottle Chess
variants.special: Chess on a Klein bottle: an 8x14 board (double-height Cylindrical Chess) where files a and h are joined (as in Cylindrical Chess), AND the rank-11/12 seam is joined with a half-twist that mirrors file position. Each side has 16 pawns across two ranks. Kings face the opponent's Queen, not the opponent's King. Bishops are not colour-bound but can reach only 3/8 of the board in one move. Invented by Alberto Monteiro.

variants.title: Knightmate
variants.special: Knight and King swap roles. The Knight is royal; Kings move as knights.

variants.title: Kriegspiel
variants.special: Fog-of-war chess. Each player sees only their own pieces. A referee manages a master board and announces partial information: legality of attempted moves, check direction, capture location, and pawn-capture availability.

variants.title: Legan Chess
variants.special: Berolina pawns (move diagonal, capture straight). King and Queen swap starting squares.

variants.title: Los Alamos Vierschach
variants.special: 4-player chess by Jörg Knappen combining Los Alamos Chess (6×6, no Bishops, no castling) with the Vierschach 4-player format. Non-competing entry to the 84 Squares Contest. Board: a 6×6 grid extended by 2×6 squares on each of the four sides, identical to the Quintessential Chess board (84 squares total). Four Los Alamos armies arranged as in Vierschach with allied teams side by side. Pawns gain initial double-step since the promotion path is longer than in standard Los Alamos; en passant applies. No castling.

variants.title: Los Alamos
variants.special: First computer chess (1956). 6x6 board, no Bishops, no castling.

variants.title: Madrasi Chess
variants.special: Same-type opposing pieces paralyse each other when they attack. Kings exempt.

variants.title: Maharaja & Sepoys
variants.special: One player has a full army. The other has one piece that moves as queen + knight.

variants.title: Makpong
variants.special: King cannot move out of check. You must block or capture instead.

variants.title: Makruk
variants.special: Thai chess. Khon moves 5 directions (silver general). Pawns promote on rank 6 to Met. No castling or en passant.

variants.title: Mansindam (Pantheon Tale)
variants.special: 9×9 board with Shogi-style drops and mandatory promotion in the enemy camp. Compound pieces: Cardinal (B+N), Marshal (R+N), Angel (Q+N). Campmate wins. Stalemate is a loss; no draws possible.

variants.title: Marseillais Chess
variants.special: Each player makes TWO moves per turn (except White's first turn).

variants.title: McCooey's Hexagonal Chess
variants.special: Same 91-hex board as Gliński, but diagonal pawn captures, 7 pawns per side, and stalemate is a draw. Invented Dave McCooey.

variants.title: Medusa Chess
variants.special: After the queen moves, all enemy pieces she attacks become petrified for 2 turns. Kings immune.

variants.title: Metamachy
variants.special: 12×12 board with 12 piece types. Variable starting position: King, Queen, Lion, Eagle may be placed in any arrangement on their four squares; Black decides, White mirrors. Cannon slides/Xiangqi-captures; Camel leaps (1,3); Eagle bends diagonal then slides orthogonal; Lion leaps anywhere within 2 King steps.

variants.title: Mini Hexchess
variants.special: 37-hex board, 7 files, no Queen piece. All 7 opponent-side hexes are promotion squares. Promotes to R/B/N only. Invented Dave McCooey, 1997.

variants.title: Minichess
variants.special: Gardner's 5x5 board. All piece types, fast tactical games.

variants.title: Möbius Strip Chess
variants.special: Chess on a Möbius strip: an 8x14 board (double-height Cylindrical Chess) where files a and h wrap normally, and the rank-11/12 seam joins with a half-twist that mirrors file position. Each side has 16 pawns across two ranks, advancing from both ends of the strip toward the middle and toward the twisted seam. Kings face the opponent's Queen, not the opponent's King. Bishops are not colour-bound. Invented by Alberto Monteiro.

variants.title: Monster Chess
variants.special: White moves twice per turn but starts with only King, Rooks, and pawns.

variants.title: No Castling Chess
variants.special: Standard chess with castling removed. Kings must develop naturally.

variants.title: No Retreat
variants.special: Pieces cannot move backward toward their own starting rank.

variants.title: Oblong Chess
variants.special: Historical chess variant on a 4×16 board (four files, sixteen ranks). Approximately one thousand years old. A variant of Shatranj — the Arabic predecessor of modern chess — using the full Shatranj piece set. Seven different starting setups are documented. Often played with dice that determine which piece type may move each turn. The extreme rectangular board shifts piece values significantly: Rooks are very strong on the long 16-rank axis.

variants.title: Omega Chess
variants.special: Commercial variant on a 10×10 board with 4 extra "wizard squares" beyond the corners (104 total squares). Adds Champion (WAD: leaps 2 ortho/diag or slides 1 ortho) and Wizard (FC: leaps (1,3)/(3,1) or slides 1 diag). Pawns may advance 1, 2, or 3 squares on first move.

variants.title: Omnicide
variants.special: Lose all your pieces to win. Captures NOT forced (unlike Antichess).

variants.title: Orda Chess
variants.special: Asymmetric: White plays standard. Black commands the Horde — divergent movers that move one way and capture another.

variants.title: Orda Mirror
variants.special: Both players command the Horde army from Orda Chess. Every piece moves as a Knight but captures as its FIDE counterpart. Designed by Corey Clark, 2020.

variants.title: Ouk Chaktrang (Cambodian Chess)
variants.special: Cambodian chess. Koul leaps 1 or 2 squares diagonally; King may jump as a Knight on its first move. Pawns promote on rank 6. Codified by the Asian Chess Federation.

variants.title: Patrol Chess
variants.special: Pieces can only capture or give check when defended by a friendly piece. Non-capturing moves unrestricted.

variants.title: Pawns Only
variants.special: Kings and pawns only. First to promote wins instantly.

variants.title: Peasants' Revolt
variants.special: White has King + 8 pawns vs Black's King + 2 Knights + 8 pawns.

variants.title: Petty Chess
variants.special: All piece types on a compact 5×6 board. Single copies of each.

variants.title: Placement Chess
variants.special: Players take turns placing their back-rank pieces before the game begins. Bishops must be on opposite-colored squares. Designed by David Bronstein; also published as a Chess Variant Pages format.

variants.title: Pocket Knight Chess
variants.special: Each player holds one extra Knight in reserve (the "pocket"). Once per game, instead of making a normal move, a player may drop their pocket Knight onto any empty square.

variants.title: Poison Chess
variants.special: Capture squares become poisoned for 3 turns — non-king pieces landing there are destroyed.

variants.title: Progressive Italian
variants.special: Italian progressive — moves escalate (1, 2, 3...) but you may not give check until your final move of the turn.

variants.title: Progressive
variants.special: Moves per turn escalate: 1, 2, 3, 4... Check ends your turn early.

variants.title: Racing Kings
variants.special: No checks allowed. Both kings start on 1st rank. Race to the top.

variants.title: Raumschach
variants.special: Three-dimensional chess on five stacked 5×5 boards. Adds the Unicorn (triagonal slider). Pawns move forward or upward; capture diagonally. No castling, no en passant, no double push.

variants.title: Recruitment Chess
variants.special: Captured pieces defect to the captor and appear on the vacated square.

variants.title: Rifle Chess
variants.special: Capturing pieces stay on their square — they 'shoot' the target.

variants.title: Rollerball
variants.win: Checkmate the King, OR King clockwise-reaches opponent's King starting square
variants.special: Chess variant on a 40-square ring board (7×7 grid with 3×3 centre removed). Two concentric rings: outer (24 squares) and inner (16 squares). Each side has only 6 pieces: King, Bishop, 2 Rooks, 2 Pawns. Pieces move clockwise-dominant (most cannot slide backward). Jean-Louis Cazaux, 1999, 40-squares contest.

variants.title: Romanchenko's Chess
variants.special: Standard FIDE chess pieces and rules on a board with 'broken columns' — certain file columns are displaced or interrupted at specific ranks, breaking the standard 8×8 grid alignment and preventing rote pattern memorization. Designed by Soviet chess trainer V. Romanchenko as a pedagogical tool: players must reason from first principles rather than imitate memorized openings. Jocly implementation on chessvariants.com.

variants.title: S-Chess (Seirawan Chess)
variants.special: Two new compound pieces — Hawk and Elephant — enter the board via a gating mechanic when back-rank pieces leave their starting squares. Designed by Yasser Seirawan and Jonathan Tisdall, 2007.

variants.title: Senterej
variants.special: Ethiopian Shatranj variant with a unique mobilization phase: before the first capture, both players move simultaneously without turns. Shatranj-style pieces (Fil leaps diagonally 2, Ferz moves 1 diagonal). No castling, no en passant.

variants.title: Shafran's Hexagonal Chess
variants.special: Smaller 70-hex board with 9 files. Castling permitted. Variable pawn initial step by file. Invented Boris Shafran.

variants.title: Shako
variants.special: 10×10 board adding the Cannon (slides to move, leaps over a platform to capture) and Elephant (leaps 2 diagonally). Designed by Jean-Louis Cazaux, 2000.

variants.title: Shatar
variants.special: Mongolian chess. Check exists (shak/dug/tsod). Mate must include a shak. Knight cannot deliver mate. Bare king is a draw. Obligatory opening 1.d4 d5.

variants.title: Shatranj Kamil
variants.special: ‘Complete Chess’ — a historical Arabic chess variant (~1000 years old) on a 10×10 board. Adds two War Machines (Dabbabah) per side to the standard Shatranj set. War Machines move as Kings but are immune to check. Unique promotion rule: a Pawn can only promote when the player has no General on the board.

variants.title: Shatranj
variants.special: Medieval Islamic chess. Bare king and stalemate are both wins. Ancestor of modern chess.

variants.title: Shinobi Chess
variants.special: Asymmetric: FIDE Kingdom vs. Shinobi Clan. Shinobi starts with fewer pieces but gains new pieces by dropping clan members held in hand. Shinobi pieces promote on reaching the promotion zone. Designed by Corey Clark, 2021.

variants.title: Shinobi+
variants.win: Checkmate or campmate (King/Kage reaches opponent's last rank)
variants.special: Rebalanced Shinobi Chess. The Clan (Pink) moves first, starts with most pieces in hand including a new Fox piece (Bishop+King hybrid). Kingdom Pawns promote on rank 6. Perpetual check is a loss. Designed by Couch Tomato, 2021.

variants.title: Shogun Chess
variants.special: Zone-triggered automatic promotion and Shogi-style drops from captured pieces. Designed by Corey Clark, 2020.

variants.title: Single-Check
variants.special: One check wins. No checkmate needed — any single check ends the game.

variants.title: Sittuyin
variants.special: Burmese chess. Placement opening phase. Pawns promote on the diagonal. No castling or en passant.

variants.title: Spartan Chess
variants.special: Asymmetric: Persian (standard FIDE) vs. Spartan army with two Kings and unique pieces. Designed by Steven Streetman, 2010.

variants.title: Spherical Chess
variants.special: Chess on a sphere — a surface with no edges and no corners, where ranks and files meet at poles. The standard 8×8 board is played with two wrapping rules: ranks wrap horizontally (left-right, as in Cylindrical Chess), and files meet at polar singularities where a piece crossing the pole continues four files away. Multiple documented versions from 1950–2014; this file documents the family and the most widely agreed rules. Bishops are colourbound. Knights have 8 possible moves from any position.

variants.title: Stalemate Wins
variants.special: Standard chess but stalemate is a win, not a draw.

variants.title: Stupidhouse
variants.special: Bughouse chess variant where received pieces are placed on a randomly selected empty square rather than a player-chosen square. When a player captures a piece, it passes to their partner — but when the partner uses it, it lands on a random legal empty square instead of a chosen one. Removes strategic drop placement and replaces it with chaos.

variants.title: Suicide Chess
variants.special: Forced captures like Giveaway, but stalemate is a draw, not a loss.

variants.title: Synochess
variants.special: Asymmetric: Western (FIDE) vs. Eastern dynasty (Xiangqi-derived pieces, Cannon, Chariot, Soldier drops). Faceoff rule ends the game if royal pieces face each other unobstructed. Designed by Corey Clark, 2020.

variants.title: Tamerlane Chess
variants.win: Checkmate (or bare king with citadel draw)
variants.special: Medieval 14th-century chess of Timur. 28 pieces per side, 12 piece types, three-stage promoting pawn, citadel draw rule.

variants.title: Tandem Chess
variants.win: Checkmate either opposing King across both boards
variants.special: Team chess variant for 2×2 players on two simultaneous boards. Captured pieces are passed to the partner for dropping on the partner's board. Also known as Siamese Chess. Key differences from Bughouse: (1) no check or checkmate by drop; (2) match continues until both games complete. Invented ~1960s.

variants.title: Teleportation Chess
variants.special: Each side has 3 teleports per game — move any piece to any empty square.

variants.title: Three-Check
variants.special: First to check the opponent three times wins.

variants.title: Toroidal Byzantine Chess
variants.board: 4-ring torus (4×16 circular board with radial wrap)
variants.special: Byzantine Chess (historical Shatranj on a 4×16 circular board) combined with toroidal topology: the innermost ring connects to the outermost ring radially, in addition to the standard circular wrap along each ring. A piece sliding inward past ring 4 emerges from ring 1; a piece sliding outward past ring 1 emerges from ring 4. Invented by Anatoly Khalfine and Ernst Saperow, circa 1999–2001.

variants.title: Gadsden's Toroidal Chess
variants.special: Chess on a torus — all four edges wrap. Moving off the right edge (h-file) reappears on the left (a-file); moving off rank 8 reappears on rank 1. Every square has exactly 8 neighbours; there are no edge squares and no corner squares. Uses a three-rank starting position per side with an extra set of pawns (32 pawns total). Invented around 1990 by Richard Gadsden and Phil Roberts as a variant of Cylindrical Chess.

variants.title: Torpedo Chess
variants.special: Pawns can move two squares forward from any rank, not just the starting rank.

variants.title: Turkish Great Chess II (Atranj)
variants.special: Historical large chess variant known as Atranj or Qatranj, described by H. J. R. Murray in A History of Chess. Played on a 10×10 board with an expanded piece set including the Prince (moves as Rook, Bishop, or Knight), Kotwal (Bishop or Knight), and Urdabegini (moves one square toward the opposing King). Despite its Turkish classification in Murray's work, the source manuscript is Indian. No castling.

variants.title: Turkish Great Chess III
variants.special: Historical large chess variant played on a 12×12 board. One of four Ottoman/Indian large chess variants catalogued by John Gollon from H. J. R. Murray's A History of Chess. Expands the standard chess piece set with multiple piece types that move as Bishop (Fil, Dahja) and adds the Chariot (Ratha, moves as Rook) alongside two Rooks. The Wazir moves as a full Queen. No castling; no Pawn double step.

variants.title: Turkish Great Chess IV
variants.special: Historical large chess variant played on a 14×14 board. Despite its Turkish classification, it includes Indian and Persian piece names (Raja, Rani, Shahzadeh) suggesting a mixed cultural origin. The Rani (Queen) is weak — moving only one square in any direction — and uniquely may be placed or left en prise without penalty. No castling; no Pawn double step.

variants.title: Ultima (Baroque Chess)
variants.special: All seven piece types use entirely different capture mechanics. No check: win by physically capturing the opponent's King. Designed by Robert Abbott, 1962.

variants.title: Upside-Down
variants.special: Pieces start on the opponent's back rank. Instant tactical chaos.

variants.title: Vierschach
variants.win: Checkmate the last surviving enemy King
variants.special: Traditional German 4-player chess invented by Dr. G. Arthur Lutze (1813–1870). Cross-shaped 160-square board. Two teams of two, allied armies placed side by side. Standard FIDE movement. First enemy King may be captured normally; second enemy King must be checkmated.

variants.title: Weak!
variants.special: Weakest piece type with a legal move must move first. Strength order: Pawn < Knight < Bishop < Rook < Queen < King.

variants.title: Xiang Fu
variants.win: Duple Checkmate, or capture one Champion then checkmate the remaining one
variants.special: Xiangqi/chess hybrid by Eventlesstew for the PyChess Variant Design Contest. 9×9 board, dual Champions (royal), Crossbow (diagonal Cannon), piece drops within first two ranks, captures go to hand.

variants.title: Yalta Chess
variants.win: Be the last player with a King remaining
variants.special: 3-player chess on a hexagonal board divided into three Y-shaped sectors, one per player (Red, Green, Blue), meeting at a central junction. Checkmating a player captures their army. Alliances encouraged.
